exact_task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n, theta a smooth real nef (1,1) background, h a smooth positive Hermitian form and mu a smooth strictly positive probability volume. Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. Nef means that for every epsilon>0 a smooth potential gives theta+epsilon h+dd^c u>0. For a smooth background A with a positive smooth potential representative define D_mu(gamma)=integral_X (mu/gamma^n)^(1/n) gamma^n and lambda_mu(A)=inf_gamma integral_X A wedge gamma^(n-1)/D_mu(gamma), where gamma is any smooth positive Gauduchon metric, dd^c gamma^(n-1)=0. Put V_mu(A)=lambda_mu(A)^n; in dimension one lambda is integral A. Define a_minus(theta)=liminf_{epsilon down0} log V_mu(theta+epsilon h)/log epsilon and a_plus using limsup.
Question: find geometric hypotheses on genuinely nonclosed nef backgrounds forcing a common degeneration order, or forcing it to be integral, and characterize equality in the modification and effective-divisorial-residual comparisons in an explicit meaningful nonclosed class. A complete sufficient-condition theorem with all geometry specified is sought; an unrestricted integer-order claim is false.
Known background: 0<=a_minus<=a_plus<=n; both are independent of mu,h, smooth dd^c gauge, and positive scale. For closed nef classes on a compact Kahler manifold they equal n minus numerical dimension. Nonclosed elliptic-product examples have unequal orders, irrational common orders, or zero volume with decay slower than every positive power. The scalar Hopf threefold's single horizontal background already has order one despite failure of bounded mass. Explicit elliptic threefold boundary ranks also give known integer examples. Merely repeating these cases does not find new conditions.
For a modification pi:Y->X of smooth compact n-folds, the known comparison is a_minus(pi*theta)>=a_minus(theta) and likewise for a_plus; it can be strict for nonclosed backgrounds. For smooth nef theta,beta with a positive current (theta-beta)+dd^c phi>=0, both residual orders are at least those of theta. Effective-divisorial removal is the special case beta=theta-eta_D for a smooth curvature representative eta_D of an effective real divisor, with [D]=eta_D+dd^c phi. The residual must remain nef. Removing a divisor from an actual boundary current is distinct from the perturbative minimal divisorial multiplicities, which vanish for nef backgrounds.
Find new proved hypotheses giving a common/integer order and a complete equality criterion within a fully specified nonclosed geometric family for both comparisons. Verify the exact volume or quantitative two-sided asymptotics from the full Gauduchon infimum; a formal determinant calculation without proving its variational relevance does not suffice. Keep the metric/background cone fixed and separate restricted criteria from arbitrary nonclosed classification. No candidate family or proof is supplied.

notes.summary: Full-Gauduchon sandwich lemma: a smooth nef background bounded above by a closed constant-rank semipositive form B and bounded below by B after an L1 dd^c potential has V_mu(theta+epsilon h) asymptotic to epsilon^(n-rank B), uniformly up to positive constants. Proof uses every Gauduchon test and an admissible closed test, not a formal determinant.
notes.detailedSummary: Let M be compact Kähler, Omega a Kähler form, and B smooth closed semipositive of constant complex rank r. If theta is smooth nef, theta<=C B, and theta+dd^c phi>=c B as currents for phi in L1, then for arbitrary smooth positive Hermitian h and probability volume mu, c' epsilon^(n-r)<=V_mu(theta+epsilon h)<=C' epsilon^(n-r), for 0<epsilon<=1. The essential point is that distributional dd^c phi integrates to zero against every smooth Gauduchon gamma^(n-1). Thus the full infimum is bounded above and below by constant multiples of the full infimum for B+epsilon Omega. Constant rank gives uniform pointwise bounds for (B+epsilon Omega)^n; AM-GM proves the lower bound for all tests, while gamma=B+epsilon Omega is closed, positive and Gauduchon and proves the upper bound. This also gives a comparison lemma when B is not constant rank; in that case it does not by itself give quantitative volume asymptotics.
notes.text:
All conventions are those in the question, in particular dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. No Monge-Ampere existence theorem is used below.

LEMMA (full-infimum sandwich). Let M be a compact complex n-fold with a Kähler form Omega. Let B be a smooth real closed semipositive (1,1) form. Let theta be a smooth nef background, and assume
  (1) theta <= C B pointwise,
  (2) theta+dd^c phi >= c B as currents,
where C,c>0 and phi is a globally defined locally integrable real function. Suppose theta+epsilon h has a smooth positive potential representative for epsilon>0, as in the question. Let mu be any smooth strictly positive probability volume and h any smooth positive Hermitian form. Then there are positive constants k,K independent of 0<epsilon<=1 such that
  k lambda_mu(B+epsilon Omega) <= lambda_mu(theta+epsilon h)
       <= K lambda_mu(B+epsilon Omega).
The same conclusion holds when theta itself is semipositive, in which case the positive-representative hypothesis is automatic.

PROOF. Compactness gives c_h Omega<=h<=C_h Omega. For every smooth positive Gauduchon gamma, distributional integration by parts gives
  integral_M dd^c phi wedge gamma^(n-1)
    = integral_M phi dd^c gamma^(n-1)=0.
The pairing is well defined because gamma is smooth and phi is locally integrable. A positive current wedged with the smooth positive form gamma^(n-1) is a positive measure. Consequently
  integral (theta+epsilon h) wedge gamma^(n-1)
    >= min(c,c_h) integral (B+epsilon Omega) wedge gamma^(n-1).
The upper inequality follows pointwise from (1) and h<=C_h Omega, with max(C,C_h). Divide by the same positive D_mu(gamma) and take the infimum over ALL positive Gauduchon gamma. This proves the comparison; no subset of tests is substituted for the prescribed cone.

If B has constant rank r, then
  k_0 epsilon^(n-r) <= V_mu(theta+epsilon h)
       <= K_0 epsilon^(n-r).
Here and below the constants can depend on the fixed background, mu and h, but not on epsilon.

For completeness, this second statement follows from the variational definition, not merely from computing a determinant. Put A_epsilon=B+epsilon Omega. The r positive eigenvalues of B with respect to Omega have a common positive lower bound and a finite upper bound, by compactness and constant rank. Hence there are L,U>0 such that
  L epsilon^(n-r) mu <= A_epsilon^n <= U epsilon^(n-r) mu,
for 0<epsilon<=1. This includes r=0.

At each point the matrix arithmetic-geometric mean inequality gives, for every positive gamma,
  A_epsilon wedge gamma^(n-1)
    >= (A_epsilon^n/gamma^n)^(1/n) gamma^n.
Using the pointwise lower volume bound and integrating proves, for EVERY positive Gauduchon test,
  integral A_epsilon wedge gamma^(n-1)
    >= L^(1/n) epsilon^((n-r)/n) D_mu(gamma).
Thus lambda_mu(A_epsilon)>=L^(1/n)epsilon^((n-r)/n).

For the upper bound take gamma=A_epsilon. It is Kähler, hence Gauduchon. Write A_epsilon^n=f_epsilon mu. Since mu(M)=1,
  D_mu(A_epsilon)=integral f_epsilon^((n-1)/n) mu
    >= L^((n-1)/n)epsilon^((n-r)(n-1)/n),
while integral A_epsilon^n<=U epsilon^(n-r). This gives
  lambda_mu(A_epsilon)<=U L^(-(n-1)/n)epsilon^((n-r)/n).
Raising to the nth power and using the sandwich comparison proves the assertion. In dimension one the same computation reduces to lambda_mu(A)=integral A, since D_mu(gamma)=integral mu=1.

In particular a_minus(theta)=a_plus(theta)=n-r. Constants in two-sided bounds disappear upon division by log epsilon. The lemma uses no bounded-mass hypothesis and does not assert anything about an arbitrary nonclosed background lacking the stated sandwich.

reconstruction.statement:
Let M be a compact complex manifold of dimension n≥1 admitting a Kähler form Ω, and use dd^c=(i/(2π))∂∂̄. Let μ be any smooth strictly positive probability volume on M and h any smooth positive Hermitian form. For a smooth real (1,1) background A admitting a smooth positive potential representative, define
D_μ(γ)=∫_M (μ/γ^n)^(1/n) γ^n,
λ_μ(A)=inf_γ [∫_M A∧γ^(n−1)]/D_μ(γ),
V_μ(A)=λ_μ(A)^n,
where the infimum is over all smooth positive Gauduchon metrics γ, namely all smooth positive Hermitian forms satisfying dd^c γ^(n−1)=0. In dimension one, λ_μ(A)=∫_M A.

Let B be a smooth real closed semipositive (1,1) form, and let θ be a smooth real nef background. Suppose that there are C,c>0 and a globally defined locally integrable real function φ such that
θ≤CB pointwise,
θ+dd^c φ≥cB as currents.
Suppose also that, for every ε>0, θ+εh admits a smooth positive potential representative, as required by nefness in the question. Then there are k,K>0, independent of 0<ε≤1, such that
k λ_μ(B+εΩ)≤λ_μ(θ+εh)≤K λ_μ(B+εΩ).
No constant-rank hypothesis on B is required for this comparison. If θ itself is semipositive, the positive-potential-representative hypothesis is automatic, and the same comparison holds under the remaining hypotheses.

If, in addition, B has constant complex rank r, where 0≤r≤n, then there are k₀,K₀>0, independent of 0<ε≤1, such that
k₀ ε^(n−r)≤V_μ(θ+εh)≤K₀ ε^(n−r).
Consequently, with
a_−(θ)=liminf_(ε↓0) log V_μ(θ+εh)/log ε,
a_+(θ)=limsup_(ε↓0) log V_μ(θ+εh)/log ε,
one has a_−(θ)=a_+(θ)=n−r. These conclusions hold for every μ and h specified above; the constants may depend on the fixed data but not on ε.
reconstruction.proof:
Write F_A(γ)=∫_M A∧γ^(n−1). All pairings below are with the entire smooth positive Gauduchon cone.

1. Comparison, including currents. Compactness and positivity give constants t,T>0 with tΩ≤h≤TΩ. Since φ is globally locally integrable, distributional integration by parts gives
∫_M dd^cφ∧γ^(n−1)=∫_M φ dd^c(γ^(n−1))=0.
The positive-current hypothesis can therefore be paired with the smooth positive form γ^(n−1), yielding F_θ(γ)≥cF_B(γ). The pointwise upper hypothesis gives F_θ(γ)≤CF_B(γ). Consequently, for every ε>0 and every admissible γ,
min(c,t)F_(B+εΩ)(γ)≤F_(θ+εh)(γ)≤max(C,T)F_(B+εΩ)(γ).
Division by the same positive D_μ(γ), followed by taking infima, proves the asserted comparison with k=min(c,t) and K=max(C,T). The backgrounds involved are admissible: B+εΩ is itself Kähler, and admissibility of θ+εh is the stated hypothesis. This argument does not require constant rank. If θ is semipositive, θ+εh is positive without any potential, so its admissibility and nefness are automatic.

2. A full-test estimate for constant-rank B. Put d=n−r and ω_ε=B+εΩ. The nonzero eigenvalues of B relative to Ω have uniform positive lower bounds and finite upper bounds: they are continuous ordered eigenvalues, their number is constantly r, and M is compact. Thus, also for r=0, there are p,P>0 such that for 0<ε≤1,
p ε^d μ≤ω_ε^n≤P ε^d μ.                         (1)
Here the comparison between the fixed smooth positive volumes Ω^n and μ has been incorporated into p,P.

For any positive (1,1) form A and positive metric γ, the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality on the eigenvalues of A relative to γ gives
A∧γ^(n−1)=(tr_γ A/n)γ^n≥(A^n/γ^n)^(1/n)γ^n.
Apply this with A=ω_ε. By (1), for every smooth positive Gauduchon metric γ,
F_(ω_ε)(γ)≥p^(1/n) ε^(d/n)∫_M μ^(1/n)(γ^n)^((n−1)/n)
=p^(1/n) ε^(d/n)D_μ(γ).
This proves the required lower bound from all tests, not from a restricted collection.

For the upper bound choose the particular test γ=ω_ε. It is admissible because ω_ε is closed, hence dd^c(ω_ε^(n−1))=0. Using ∫_M μ=1 and (1),
F_(ω_ε)(ω_ε)=∫_M ω_ε^n≤P ε^d,
D_μ(ω_ε)=∫_M (ω_ε^n/μ)^((n−1)/n)μ≥p^((n−1)/n)ε^(d(n−1)/n).
Therefore
p^(1/n)ε^(d/n)≤λ_μ(B+εΩ)≤P p^(−(n−1)/n)ε^(d/n).
Combining this with part 1 and raising to the nth power gives positive constants k₀,K₀ with
k₀ε^(n−r)≤V_μ(θ+εh)≤K₀ε^(n−r).
Taking logarithms gives log V_μ(θ+εh)=(n−r)log ε+O(1), proving both orders equal n−r.

In dimension one, γ^0=1 and D_μ(γ)=∫μ=1; hence λ_μ(A)=∫A. The same current pairing and estimates apply, and the displayed arithmetic–geometric mean inequality is an equality. Thus dimension one and the endpoint ranks r=0,n are included. No Monge–Ampère existence theorem or exact closed-volume formula was used.

notes.summary: Explicit projective nonclosed family with integer orders: products of projective spaces and blowups of projective spaces along linear subspaces, with fixed positive-function coefficient cones in the forms H=pi*FS and Q=q*FS. A block with an active H contributes its full dimension; with Q only it contributes dim q-base; with neither it contributes zero. An explicit exceptional-divisor potential supplies the current sandwich needed for the full-infimum proof.
notes.detailedSummary: For Y=Bl_{P^ell}P^m, 0<=ell<=m-2, describe Y as the graph of the rational complementary-coordinate map q:P^m-->P^(m-ell-1). Then q is a smooth P^(ell+1)-bundle, H=pi*omega_m and Q=q*omega_r are semipositive and closed, Q has constant rank r=m-ell-1, and kappa=H+Q is Kähler. The exceptional divisor satisfies O(E)=pi*O(1) tensor q*O(-1), so with the induced metric, dd^c psi_E=[E]-H+Q and H+dd^c(psi_E/2)=(kappa+[E])/2. On a product of such factors and plain projective factors, fix strictly positive smooth functions f_i,g_i once and for all, and the cone theta=sum ((a_i+b_i f_i)H_i+(c_i+d_i g_i)Q_i), coefficients nonnegative (Q omitted on plain factors). Every background is smooth semipositive and nef for every h. Define R_i=m_i if H active; R_i=r_i if Q only is active; R_i=0 otherwise. A closed constant-rank comparison form is the sum of kappa_i on H-active blocks and Q_i on Q-only blocks. Pointwise upper and divisorial-current lower bounds prove the n1 hypotheses, hence V_mu(theta+epsilon h) is two-sided comparable to epsilon^(n-sum R_i). The cone contains genuinely nonclosed backgrounds; nonclosedness cannot be removed by dd^c gauge.
notes.text:
This gives a completely specified geometric family. The elementary geometric facts used here are reconstructed directly, so there is no unverified external existence or volume theorem.

I. THE FACTORS.
(A) A plain factor is Z=P^m, m>=1, with normalized Fubini-Study form H=omega_m, the curvature of O(1) with its standard metric. Put kappa=H; there is no Q generator.
(B) A blown factor has m>=2 and 0<=ell<=m-2. Let L=P^ell be the coordinate linear subspace of P^m with coordinates [z_0:...:z_ell:w_0:...:w_(m-ell-1)] and equations w=0. Put r=m-ell-1 (so 1<=r<m). Define
  Z={(x,[t_0:...:t_r]) in P^m x P^r : w_a t_b=w_b t_a for all a,b}.
Let pi:Z->P^m and q:Z->P^r be the projections. This is the blowup of L: on a chart t_j!=0 the equations are w_a=t_a w_j (with t_j=1), which are precisely the usual blowup charts for the ideal (w_0,...,w_r). These charts also show smoothness. For fixed [t], write w=lambda t; the remaining homogeneous coordinates [z_0:...:z_ell:lambda] give a fiber P^(ell+1). The local t-chart descriptions trivialize these fibers, so q is a holomorphic submersion, with rank r.

Set H=pi*omega_m, Q=q*omega_r, and kappa=H+Q. H and Q are closed semipositive. Q has constant rank r. The inclusion of Z into P^m x P^r is a smooth holomorphic embedding, and the sum of the two Fubini-Study forms on that product is positive; therefore kappa is Kähler.

The exceptional divisor E is {w=0}. The coordinate section w_j of pi*O(1) has divisor E+q^{-1}{t_j=0}, with the identity understood in every blowup chart. Thus
  O(E)=pi*O(1) tensor q*O(-1).
Equip this line bundle with the product metric, of curvature H-Q. For its canonical section s_E, put psi_E=log|s_E|^2. With the normalization in the question the Poincare-Lelong calculation is
  dd^c psi_E=[E]-H+Q.
One can check the normalization locally from dd^c log|z|^2=[z=0], whose coefficient is one by integration on a transverse disc; the metric term contributes minus the curvature. The logarithms are locally integrable. In particular
  H+dd^c(psi_E/2)=(H+Q+[E])/2 >= kappa/2.       (*)
This explicit current identity, not a big-class existence theorem, is the fact needed below.

II. THE FIXED BACKGROUND CONE.
Let X=product_{i=1}^s Z_i be any product of factors of the above two types. Write m_i=dim Z_i and n=sum m_i. Forms from factors are always pulled back to X. Fix ONCE AND FOR ALL smooth strictly positive real functions f_i on X and, for every blown factor, g_i on X. The functions may depend on any of the product coordinates. They do not depend on epsilon, mu, h, the divisor, or the cone parameters. Define the fixed finite-dimensional cone C_X by
  theta=sum_i ((a_i+b_i f_i)H_i+(c_i+d_i g_i)Q_i),
where a_i,b_i,c_i,d_i>=0. On plain factors the Q term and its parameters are omitted. All forms, metrics and generating functions are fixed before choosing parameters. This is a cone of smooth backgrounds, not a restriction on the Gauduchon test metrics.

Every theta in C_X is semipositive. Therefore theta+epsilon h is itself positive, without adding any potential, for every epsilon>0 and every smooth positive Hermitian h. All these backgrounds are nef in exactly the sense of the question.

Let H_i be ACTIVE if a_i+b_i>0. On a blown factor let Q_i be active if c_i+d_i>0. Positivity of the fixed functions ensures that an active coefficient has a strictly positive uniform lower bound; it never has an isolated or partial zero. Define the effective block rank
  R_i(theta)=m_i                       if H_i is active;
  R_i(theta)=r_i=m_i-ell_i-1           if H_i is inactive and Q_i active;
  R_i(theta)=0                         otherwise.
On a plain factor only the first and last alternatives occur. Set R(theta)=sum_i R_i(theta).

THE INTEGER-ORDER ASSERTION.
For every theta in this fixed cone, every smooth positive h, and every smooth strictly positive probability mu, there are constants 0<A<=B<infinity such that
  A epsilon^(n-R(theta)) <= V_mu(theta+epsilon h)
     <= B epsilon^(n-R(theta))                 (0<epsilon<=1).
Consequently both orders exist and equal the integer n-R(theta).

PROOF FROM THE FULL INFIMUM. Define a closed comparison form B_theta as follows: on an H-active block take kappa_i; on a Q-only block take Q_i; on an inactive block take 0. Sum these forms on X. It is semipositive and has constant rank R(theta). Also Omega=sum_i kappa_i is Kähler.

For the upper pointwise bound, on an H-active blown block H_i,Q_i<=kappa_i. Coefficient functions have finite upper bounds. On a Q-only block the summand is a bounded positive function times Q_i. On a plain active block H_i=kappa_i. Thus theta<=C B_theta for some fixed C>0.

For the lower current bound, let u_i=min_X(a_i+b_i f_i)>0 on each H-active blown block. Add to theta the dd^c of the global L1 function sum_i u_i psi_(E_i)/2 over precisely those blocks. The nonnegative remainder (a_i+b_i f_i-u_i)H_i and all Q terms are untouched. By (*) the result is at least sum_i (u_i/2)kappa_i on these blocks, with additional positive divisor currents. On each H-active plain block theta>=min(a_i+b_i f_i)kappa_i. On each Q-only block it is at least min(c_i+d_i g_i)Q_i. Taking the least of the finitely many positive constants gives
  theta+dd^c phi>=c B_theta.
If every block is inactive then theta=B_theta=0 and phi=0. The full-infimum sandwich and quantitative estimate proved in n1 now apply. In particular all claimed determinants have their variational relevance proved by the all-test AM-GM lower bound and an admissible closed Gauduchon upper test.

III. GENUINE NONCLOSEDNESS.
This cone is not simply a closed cone disguised by a gauge. Its exterior derivative is
  d theta=sum_i b_i df_i wedge H_i+sum_i d_i dg_i wedge Q_i.
Choose the fixed functions so at least one of these forms is nonzero; take a background with a nonzero corresponding coefficient and no cancellation. For example, on a blown factor choose g>0 with nonzero derivative along a q-fiber in a local trivializing chart and extend it by a small smooth bump perturbation of 1. Since r>=1, dg wedge Q is then nonzero. The background gQ is smooth semipositive, genuinely nonclosed, and has order ell+1. Its nonclosedness cannot be eliminated by adding dd^c u, since d dd^c u=0. On a product, fH_1 with f>0 varying on a different factor is another explicit nonclosed example, with any desired inactive-factor contribution to the order. These are projective blowup/product families, not the listed Hopf or elliptic-product isolated examples.

reconstruction.statement:
Use dd^c=(i/(2π))∂∂̄ and the full-Gauduchon definitions of D_μ, λ_μ, V_μ and a_−,a_+ from the question.

A plain factor is Z=P^m, m≥1, with H=ω_m, the normalized Fubini–Study form given by the standard metric on O(1), and κ=H. There is no Q generator on a plain factor.

A blown factor is specified by integers m≥2 and 0≤ℓ≤m−2. Set r=m−ℓ−1, so 1≤r<m. In homogeneous coordinates [z₀:⋯:z_ℓ:w₀:⋯:w_r] on P^m, let L=P^ℓ be the coordinate subspace w=0, and define
Z={(x,[t₀:⋯:t_r])∈P^m×P^r : w_a t_b=w_b t_a for all a,b}.
Let π:Z→P^m and q:Z→P^r be the projections. Then Z is the smooth blowup Bl_L P^m, its inclusion in P^m×P^r is a smooth holomorphic embedding, and q is a holomorphically locally trivial P^(ℓ+1)-bundle, in particular a holomorphic submersion of rank r. Set
H=π*ω_m, Q=q*ω_r, κ=H+Q.
The forms H,Q are smooth closed semipositive, Q has constant complex rank r, and κ is Kähler.

Let E={w=0} be the exceptional divisor. For each j=0,…,r, the pulled-back coordinate section w_j of π*O(1) has divisor E+q^−1{t_j=0}. There is an isomorphism
O(E)=π*O(1)⊗q*O(−1).
Equip O(E) with the induced product metric, whose curvature is H−Q. For the canonical section s_E, the function ψ_E=log|s_E|² is globally defined and locally integrable, and
 dd^c ψ_E=[E]−H+Q,
 H+dd^c(ψ_E/2)=(H+Q+[E])/2≥κ/2
as currents, where [E] denotes the positive integration current of E.

Let X=∏_(i=1)^s Z_i be any finite product of these two types of factors, put m_i=dim Z_i and n=∑_i m_i, and pull all factor forms and divisors back to X. Fix once and for all smooth strictly positive real functions f_i on X and, on every blown block, g_i on X. These functions may depend on any product coordinates and are independent of ε, μ, h, the divisor and the cone parameters. The fixed finite-dimensional cone of backgrounds is
C_X={θ=∑_i [(a_i+b_i f_i)H_i+(c_i+d_i g_i)Q_i] : a_i,b_i,c_i,d_i≥0},
with all Q terms and their parameters omitted on plain factors. This cone restricts backgrounds only: every λ_μ is still the infimum over the entire smooth positive Gauduchon cone.

Every θ∈C_X is smooth semipositive. For every smooth positive Hermitian h and every ε>0, θ+εh itself is smooth positive. Thus every member of C_X is nef in the sense that, for each ε>0, θ+εh+dd^c u>0 for some smooth u.

Call H_i active if a_i+b_i>0, and, on blown blocks, call Q_i active if c_i+d_i>0. Each active coefficient function has a strictly positive uniform lower bound on X; each inactive coefficient is identically zero. Define the effective block rank by
R_i(θ)=m_i if H_i is active;
R_i(θ)=r_i=m_i−ℓ_i−1 if H_i is inactive and Q_i is active;
R_i(θ)=0 otherwise.
On a plain block only the first and last alternatives occur. Set R(θ)=∑_i R_i(θ).

Define B_θ by taking κ_i on every H-active block, Q_i on every Q-only active block, and zero on every inactive block, and summing these forms on X. Then B_θ is smooth closed semipositive of constant complex rank R(θ), and Ω=∑_i κ_i is Kähler. For every θ∈C_X there are C,c>0 such that θ≤CB_θ pointwise and θ+dd^c φ_θ≥cB_θ as currents. An explicit globally locally integrable φ_θ is
φ_θ=∑_(i blown and H-active) (u_i/2)ψ_(E_i),
where u_i=min_X(a_i+b_i f_i)>0. If all blocks are inactive, θ=B_θ=0 and φ_θ=0.

For every θ∈C_X, every smooth positive Hermitian h and every smooth strictly positive probability volume μ, there are 0<A≤B<∞, independent of 0<ε≤1, such that
A ε^(n−R(θ))≤V_μ(θ+εh)≤B ε^(n−R(θ)).
Consequently a_−(θ)=a_+(θ)=n−R(θ), an integer. The constants may depend on the fixed data, μ and h, but not on ε.

The exterior derivative of a cone member is
 dθ=∑_i b_i df_i∧H_i+∑_(i blown) d_i dg_i∧Q_i.
Whenever this expression is nonzero, θ is genuinely nonclosed; adding a smooth dd^c potential cannot make it closed. If at least one fixed form df_i∧H_i or dg_i∧Q_i is nonzero, the cone contains a genuinely nonclosed member obtained by activating the corresponding generator alone.

On a single blown factor there exist fixed smooth positive g with nonzero derivative in a q-fiber direction and dg∧Q≠0. For any such g, the background gQ is smooth semipositive, genuinely nonclosed, nef, and satisfies a_−(gQ)=a_+(gQ)=ℓ+1. On a product with at least two factors, choosing a fixed positive f that depends nontrivially on a factor different from Z_i gives the genuinely nonclosed background fH_i, with all other summands zero and common order n−m_i. Thus inactive factors can contribute arbitrary dimensions to the order within these products. These assertions are restricted to the stated fixed family and impose no integer-order conclusion on arbitrary nonclosed nef backgrounds.
reconstruction.proof:
We first establish the geometry and the current identity, then apply w7-1/n1.

1. The incidence variety. On the chart t_a≠0, normalize t_a=1. The equations defining Z read w_b=u t_b, where u=w_a. Thus the fiber over t consists of points [z₀:⋯:z_ℓ:u], and the map
(t,[z:u])↦([z:u t],t)
identifies q^(−1){t_a≠0} holomorphically with {t_a≠0}×P^(ℓ+1). These charts prove that Z is smooth, q is a holomorphically locally trivial P^(ℓ+1)-bundle, and dq has complex rank r. They also exhibit the incidence inclusion as an injective immersion; it is an embedding since Z is compact.

Away from w=0, the incidence equations force t=[w], so π is an isomorphism there. Near a point of L choose a chart z_k≠0 and normalize z_k=1. The normal coordinates to L are w₀,…,w_r. On t_a≠0 the map π is exactly
(z,u,(t_b)_(b≠a))↦(z,w_a=u,w_b=u t_b).
These are the coordinate blowup charts of the ideal (w₀,…,w_r), with their usual transitions obtained by changing the nonzero t coordinate. They identify Z with Bl_L P^m and show that E is the smooth divisor u=0. The variety is connected, as is also clear from the bundle charts.

The forms H and Q are pullbacks of positive closed Fubini–Study forms, so are smooth closed semipositive. Since q is a submersion, Q has constant rank r. The form H+Q is the restriction of the product Fubini–Study metric through the embedding Z→P^m×P^r. Its value on every nonzero tangent vector is positive; thus κ=H+Q is Kähler. The corresponding statements on a plain factor are immediate.

2. Exceptional divisor and normalization. The pulled-back section w_j of π*O(1), in the above charts, factors as u t_j. Its zero divisor is therefore E+q^(−1){t_j=0}, with multiplicity one for each component. This gives
O(E)=π*O(1)⊗q*O(−1).
The induced product metric has curvature H−Q because curvatures add under tensor products and change sign under duals.

Here the required logarithmic current identity can be checked directly for the smooth divisor E; no premise from a later note is needed. In one complex variable, Green's formula on shrinking circles gives Δlog|z|²=4πδ₀, and hence, with the normalization in the question, dd^c log|z|²=[0]. Applying this in the transverse coordinate and using integration in the remaining coordinates gives dd^c log|u|²=[u=0]. In a local nonvanishing frame e of O(E), the canonical section is u e up to a nowhere-zero holomorphic factor. Therefore log|s_E|² is locally integrable and
 dd^c log|s_E|²=[E]+dd^c log|e|²=[E]−H+Q.
The local expressions are those of a global function ψ_E=log|s_E|². It follows that
H+dd^c(ψ_E/2)=(H+Q+[E])/2≥κ/2.
The same calculation holds after pullback to a product by its factor projection; the resulting divisor is still smooth.

3. The fixed cone and the comparison background. Let
α_i=a_i+b_i f_i,   ν_i=c_i+d_i g_i
on blown blocks, omitting ν_i on plain blocks. Positivity of the fixed functions and compactness imply that α_i is identically zero exactly when a_i+b_i=0, and otherwise u_i=min_X α_i>0. Similarly ν_i is zero exactly when c_i+d_i=0, and otherwise v_i=min_X ν_i>0. All these coefficient functions have finite upper bounds. Thus every θ in the stated cone is smooth semipositive, and θ+εh is itself positive for every positive h and every ε>0. This verifies all the smooth-nef and positive-representative requirements.

The product form Ω=∑κ_i is Kähler. The form B_θ is closed and semipositive. Its summands act on separate tangent-factor summands. On an H-active block its rank is m_i, on a Q-only block its rank is r_i, and otherwise it is zero. Consequently B_θ has constant rank R(θ).

The upper comparison follows blockwise. On an H-active blown block, H_i,Q_i≤κ_i, so α_iH_i+ν_iQ_i is bounded above by a fixed multiple of κ_i. On a plain H-active block it is bounded above by a multiple of H_i. On a Q-only block it is bounded above by a multiple of Q_i. Inactive blocks contribute nothing. Taking the maximum of finitely many bounds proves θ≤CB_θ.

For the lower current comparison, use exactly the function specified in the note,
φ_θ=∑_(blown H-active i)(u_i/2)ψ_(E_i).
It is globally locally integrable. On an H-active blown block the preceding identity gives the exact decomposition
α_iH_i+ν_iQ_i+dd^c((u_i/2)ψ_(E_i))
=(α_i−u_i)H_i+ν_iQ_i+(u_i/2)(κ_i+[E_i]).
All terms on the right are positive, so the block dominates (u_i/2)κ_i. A plain H-active block dominates u_iH_i, and a Q-only block dominates v_iQ_i. The minimum of these finitely many positive constants provides c>0 with θ+dd^cφ_θ≥cB_θ. If there are no active blocks, θ=B_θ=0 and φ_θ=0; take any positive C,c.

All hypotheses of w7-1/n1 are now checked on the compact Kähler manifold X, with B=B_θ and Ω=∑κ_i. That result, which uses the full Gauduchon infimum, gives constants A,B>0 such that
Aε^(n−R(θ))≤V_μ(θ+εh)≤Bε^(n−R(θ))   (0<ε≤1),
for every prescribed smooth strictly positive probability μ and positive Hermitian h. It follows that a_−(θ)=a_+(θ)=n−R(θ). The geometric forms, functions and background cone have not been changed to obtain these estimates; only constants in the estimates depend on the chosen data.

4. Nonclosedness and examples. Since H_i and Q_i are closed, differentiation gives exactly
 dθ=∑_i b_i df_i∧H_i+∑_(blown i)d_i dg_i∧Q_i.
A nonzero value of this exterior derivative proves genuine nonclosedness. For any smooth u, d(dd^cu)=0, so a smooth potential cannot change it. If one of the displayed fixed generator derivatives is nonzero, choose only its variable-coefficient parameter positive to obtain a genuinely nonclosed cone member.

On a blown factor choose a point and bundle coordinates for q. There is a nonzero vertical real covector ξ at that point, while Q is a nonzero horizontal two-form because r≥1. Thus ξ∧Q≠0. A smooth real function supported in the coordinate neighborhood can be arranged to have differential ξ there. Adding a sufficiently large constant produces a global positive smooth g with dg∧Q≠0. The member gQ is consequently genuinely nonclosed, smooth semipositive and nef; its effective rank is r and its order is m−r=ℓ+1.

On a product of at least two factors, take a positive smooth function f pulled back from a different factor and with df nonzero somewhere. The form H_i is nonzero somewhere on Z_i (on a blown block one can choose a point outside E_i). In the direct sum of tangent-factor spaces, a nonzero one-form from the other factor wedges nontrivially with this two-form. Hence df∧H_i≠0 somewhere. The background fH_i is genuinely nonclosed, has R=m_i, and therefore has common order n−m_i. This also verifies the stated role of inactive factors. All these statements concern precisely the fixed background family, while every variational infimum remains over all Gauduchon metrics.

notes.summary: Complete restricted sufficient-condition theorem and equality criteria. In the fixed projective cone of n2, product linear blowup modifications always preserve orders; more generally every modification with Kähler source preserves them using only the closed-nef order fact supplied in the question plus full-test sandwiching. Effective divisors with fixed standard curvature and residual remaining in the cone have equality exactly when no H-leading block is erased and no Q-only block is erased. Explicit nonclosed theta=tH+gQ on Bl_{P^ell}P^m has equality after sE removal iff s<t, and at s=t its order jumps by ell+1.
notes.detailedSummary: For the n2 cone, define effective real divisors as nonnegative real sums of divisors of nonzero holomorphic sections of tensor products of the fixed O(H_i),O(Q_i), using their fixed induced metrics. Their smooth curvature is eta_D=sum(delta_i H_i+rho_i Q_i). Effectivity forces delta_i>=0 and delta_i+rho_i>=0 on blown blocks, delta_i>=0 on plain blocks; these ranges are also realized by E and Q hyperplane divisors. If a_i>=delta_i and c_i>=rho_i, the residual beta=theta-eta_D remains in the SAME cone, smooth semipositive and nef. Its parameters are a_i-delta_i,b_i,c_i-rho_i,d_i. Therefore its order is n-R(beta), and equality holds precisely when each initially H-active block retains H and each initially Q-only block retains Q. Rank decreases blockwise, so no cross-block cancellation can conceal a strict inequality. Section log-norms give the required actual positive boundary current and distinguish this operation from perturbative minimal multiplicities. Product modifications replacing plain P^m factors by the specified linear blowups preserve all block ranks and hence always give equality, quantitatively and without external analytic theorems. For an arbitrary modification with Kähler source, pulling back the explicit logarithmic-current sandwich compares the full infimum with that of pi*B_theta; this closed nef form has numerical dimension R(theta), so the supplied closed-nef theorem gives equality. No claim is made for arbitrary non-Kähler sources or arbitrary residuals outside the fixed cone. An explicit sharp nonclosed exceptional-removal example realizes every jump 1,...,m-1.
notes.text:
COMPLETE SUFFICIENT-CONDITION AND EQUALITY THEOREM.

Use precisely the factors, fixed forms, fixed positive functions and fixed cone C_X specified in n2. This theorem is a restricted result, not a classification of arbitrary nonclosed nef backgrounds. All Gauduchon infima below use the entire prescribed smooth positive Gauduchon cone. Both mu and h are arbitrary as in the question.

(1) INTEGER ORDER. Every background theta in C_X has the quantitative two-sided estimate
  V_mu(theta+epsilon h) asymptotic up to positive fixed constants to epsilon^(n-R(theta)),
with R(theta) given blockwise in n2. Thus a_minus=a_plus=n-R(theta). This includes genuinely nonclosed backgrounds with orders 0 through n-1 in suitable dimensions and products. The full-infimum proof and the smooth-nef verification are in n1 and n2.

(2) MODIFICATION COMPARISON: AN ENTIRE SELF-CONTAINED CLASS WITH EQUALITY.
Take X to be any product of the factors of n2, and replace any collection of its plain P^{m_i} factors by Bl_{P^{ell_i}}P^{m_i}, 0<=ell_i<=m_i-2; leave the other factors unchanged. Let pi:Y->X be the resulting product modification. On Y use the fixed pullbacks of the old functions and forms; fix arbitrary positive functions for any newly available Q generators, once and for all. The pullback of the old cone embeds into the new fixed cone with zero coefficients on those new Q generators. No background or test cone is varied as epsilon changes.

For every theta in C_X,
  a_minus(pi*theta)=a_plus(pi*theta)=a_minus(theta)=a_plus(theta)=n-R(theta).
Indeed a plain active H block of dimension m_i becomes an active H block of the same effective rank m_i; an inactive block remains inactive; all other blocks remain unchanged. Apply the n2 estimates on both products. In particular the equality criterion in this product-modification class is unconditional: every allowed modification and every allowed background gives equality. This remains a substantive statement when the background is degenerate and genuinely nonclosed, and when pi*H loses pointwise rank on the exceptional divisor. The exceptional-divisor logarithmic potential, rather than a claim of constant pointwise rank of pi*H, is what proves the lower variational bound.

There is a stronger extension, if one uses the closed-nef order result expressly GIVEN in the question. For theta in C_X and ANY holomorphic modification pi:Y->X with Y compact Kähler, equality again always holds. Here is the complete reduction to that supplied premise. Let B=B_theta be the closed constant-rank comparison form from n2. Its current lower-bound potential is a sum of constant multiples of logarithms of canonical divisor sections. Such logarithms pull back to logarithms of nonzero holomorphic sections; they are locally integrable and their divisor currents remain positive. Alternatively, pull back the explicit identities in n2, including the smooth nonnegative remainder terms. Hence
  pi*theta <= C pi*B,
  pi*theta+dd^c(phi composed with pi) >= c pi*B.
The smooth background pi*theta is semipositive, so pi*theta+epsilon h_Y is positive for every h_Y>0. Choose a Kähler Omega_Y. The full-test comparison in n1, which does NOT require constant rank for its comparison part, gives
  k lambda_(mu_Y)(pi*B+epsilon Omega_Y)
    <=lambda_(mu_Y)(pi*theta+epsilon h_Y)
    <=K lambda_(mu_Y)(pi*B+epsilon Omega_Y).
The numerical dimension of the smooth closed nef pi*B is R(theta): (pi*B)^(R+1)=0 identically, while (pi*B)^R wedge Omega_Y^(n-R) has strictly positive integral because pi is an isomorphism over a nonempty open set where B has rank R. The closed-nef Kähler order fact supplied in the problem therefore gives both orders n-R on Y. This extension uses that supplied fact, not an unverified external Monge-Ampere assertion. The self-contained product-modification assertion above does not need even this premise and has quantitative two-sided estimates. No claim is made here about arbitrary non-Kähler sources outside the specified product class.

(3) EFFECTIVE-DIVISOR COMPARISON IN THE SAME FIXED CONE.
The divisor family and its curvature representatives are fixed as follows. On a plain factor use the line bundle O(H_i)=O(1) with its fixed Fubini-Study metric. On a blown factor use O(H_i)=pi_i*O(1) and O(Q_i)=q_i*O(1), with their fixed pullback metrics. Consider any tensor product on X of integer powers of these bundles, permitting negative powers. Give it the induced tensor-product metric. Let
  D=sum_nu t_nu div(s_nu),  t_nu>=0,
where s_nu is a nonzero holomorphic section of one of these tensor products. This is a fully specified class of effective real divisors: it includes arbitrary hypersurfaces in these linear systems, exceptional divisors, and their nonnegative real sums. In particular it is not limited to divisors with a prescribed support. Its smooth curvature representative is fixed by the indicated metrics and is
  eta_D=sum_i (delta_i H_i+rho_i Q_i),
with Q terms omitted on plain factors. Real coefficients are obtained by adding the corresponding integer bundle exponents with weights t_nu. Set
  Phi_D=sum_nu t_nu log|s_nu|^2.
Direct Poincare-Lelong gives
  [D]=eta_D+dd^c Phi_D>=0.
The normalizations and local integrability are as checked in n2. Thus this comparison is removal from an ACTUAL positive current.

The numerical range of these effective coefficients is explicit. On plain factors delta_i>=0. On blown factors
  delta_i>=0,       delta_i+rho_i>=0.                 (**)
For a nonzero section, restrict at a generic choice of all other product coordinates. On a blown factor a generic q_i-fiber is P^{ell_i+1}, with H_i of degree one and Q_i of degree zero on its lines. A restriction that is not identically zero proves that the H exponent is nonnegative. A generic projective line in P^{m_i} disjoint from the center has a lift on which H_i and Q_i both have degree one. Such lines sweep an open subset, so one can choose a line on which the section does not vanish identically. The sum of the H and Q exponents is consequently nonnegative. The same line argument gives delta_i>=0 on plain factors. Taking nonnegative real sums proves (**). Conversely every real pair delta>=0, delta+rho>=0 is realized numerically by delta E+(delta+rho) times a Q-hyperplane divisor, since E has curvature H-Q. On a plain factor the nonnegative range is realized by hyperplanes. Thus the range just used is neither accidental nor an extra positivity assumption silently imposed on the divisor.

Let theta have cone parameters a_i,b_i,c_i,d_i. Impose the explicit cone-preserving residual conditions
  a_i>=delta_i                    on every factor,
  c_i>=rho_i                      on every blown factor.       (***)
A negative rho_i causes no difficulty. Define
  beta=theta-eta_D.
Then beta belongs to the SAME fixed cone, with parameters
  (a_i',b_i',c_i',d_i')=(a_i-delta_i,b_i,c_i-rho_i,d_i).
This is a smooth semipositive form, hence is nef for every h, with beta+epsilon h itself positive. All smooth-nef requirements are therefore verified rather than assumed after the calculation. Moreover
  (theta-beta)+dd^c Phi_D=[D]>=0,
which is exactly the effective-divisorial-residual relation in the question.

The residual orders and their gap are
  a_minus(beta)=a_plus(beta)=n-R(beta),
  a(beta)-a(theta)=sum_i (R_i(theta)-R_i(beta)).        (****)
Here a denotes the common order already proved, not a new invariant.

PRECISE EQUALITY CRITERION.
Equality holds in both residual-order comparisons if and only if BOTH of the following conditions hold:
  • Every initially H-active block retains H:
       a_i-delta_i+b_i>0 whenever a_i+b_i>0.
  • Every initially Q-only active block retains Q:
       c_i-rho_i+d_i>0 whenever a_i=b_i=0 and c_i+d_i>0.
The second condition applies only on blown factors. On H-active blocks the Q coefficient can disappear or increase without affecting equality.

PROOF OF NECESSITY AS WELL AS SUFFICIENCY. If an H-active block loses H, its old effective rank is m_i and its new rank is either r_i<m_i or zero (or zero on a plain factor), so its rank strictly decreases. If H was initially absent, then a_i=b_i=0. Conditions (**) and (***) force delta_i=0 and rho_i>=0. Hence an initially inactive block cannot gain Q, and a Q-only block can only keep or lose its rank r_i. Consequently R_i(beta)<=R_i(theta) separately on every block. There can be no cancellation between a rank loss in one block and a rank gain in another. Formula (****) now gives exactly the stated criterion. This proves a complete equality characterization within the specified fixed background and divisor cones, with no claim that (***) characterizes nefness outside that cone.

(4) SHARP GENUINELY NONCLOSED EXAMPLES AND ACTUAL BOUNDARY REMOVAL.
On the single blown factor Z=Bl_{P^ell}P^m let r=m-ell-1 and choose a fixed smooth positive g with dg wedge Q!=0, as constructed in n2. For t>0 put
  theta_t=tH+gQ.
It is genuinely nonclosed and positive: theta_t>=min(t,min g)(H+Q)>0. Thus its order is zero. For 0<=s<=t remove the effective divisor sE with the FIXED curvature eta_(sE)=s(H-Q). The residual is
  beta_s=(t-s)H+(g+s)Q,
which is smooth semipositive, nef, and still genuinely nonclosed. The theorem gives
  a(beta_s)=0             for s<t,
  a(beta_t)=m-r=ell+1     for s=t.
Thus equality is precisely s<t, while exact removal of the H coefficient produces the integer jump ell+1. As ell ranges from 0 to m-2 this realizes all jumps 1,...,m-1, not merely a single threefold case.

The associated actual positive boundary current is explicit:
  theta_t+dd^c(s psi_E)
      =s[E]+(t-s)H+(g+s)Q.
After removing s[E] its smooth residual is beta_s. At s=t all of the effective mass t[E] is present in this chosen boundary current. This says nothing about minimal perturbative divisorial multiplicities: for these nef forms beta_s+epsilon h and theta_t+epsilon h are smooth positive, so their minimal perturbative multiplicities are zero. The two notions are visibly distinct here.

For genuinely nonclosed examples with nonzero degeneration order and modification equality, take X=P^p x P^q, p,q>=1, a fixed positive f depending nontrivially on the second factor, and theta=f H_1. Then dtheta=df wedge H_1!=0, its order is q, and every allowed product linear blowup has the same order; every modification with Kähler source has the same order by the supplied closed-nef extension. This includes nontrivial blowups of both the active and inactive directions.

SCOPE AND COMPLETENESS. This is a complete sufficient-condition answer: the geometry, background cone, divisor cone, curvature representatives and residual-nef conditions are all explicit; quantitative full-infimum bounds prove common integer orders; modification equality and a necessary-and-sufficient effective-divisorial equality criterion are proved in the stated family. The proof does not invoke a formal determinant without an all-test argument, an averaging restriction, bounded mass, or a new external analytic premise. The optional arbitrary-Kähler-modification extension uses only the closed-nef order theorem already included among the problem's known facts, after proving its variational reduction. There is no unrestricted integer-order claim and no equality classification for backgrounds, residuals or non-Kähler modifications outside these hypotheses.

correctness.report:

For an arbitrary modification with Kähler source, the logarithmic potentials pull back through nonzero holomorphic sections, avoiding an unjustified pullback of a general L1 potential. The pulled-back comparison form has numerical dimension R: its next wedge power vanishes, and its Rth power has a positive Kähler intersection on the isomorphism locus. The task-granted closed-nef order theorem therefore applies. This extension proves orders, not an additional two-sided power estimate.

The effective coefficient constraints follow from restriction to q-fibers and lifted lines avoiding the center; exceptional and Q-hyperplane divisors realize the converse range. Under (***) the residual remains smooth semipositive in the fixed cone. When H was absent, effectivity forces delta=0 and rho>=0, so block ranks cannot increase. Consequently equality is exactly preservation of every H-active block and every Q-only active block, with no possible cross-block cancellation. The examples, signs, jump sizes, and distinction between actual boundary removal and perturbative minimal multiplicities are correct. The summaries preserve the restricted-family scope; the detailed summary explicitly retains (***) and the Kähler-source limitation. General Poincaré–Lelong for possibly singular divisors and total transforms is the additional nonroutine premise requiring source validation.

requirements.report:
The theorem follows from the established n1/n2 results with their hypotheses satisfied. The backgrounds, pullbacks, and permitted residuals are smooth semipositive, hence nef for every positive h. The quantitative estimates use the full Gauduchon infimum, with constants independent of epsilon; no product-test restriction or determinant-only argument is introduced.

The modification arguments are valid. Allowed product modifications preserve every effective block rank. For the optional Kähler-source extension, the explicit section-log potentials pull back as locally integrable functions with positive divisor currents. The resulting full-infimum sandwich applies to pi*B, whose numerical dimension is exactly R: its higher wedge powers vanish, while its R-th power has positive pairing on the isomorphism locus. The supplied closed-nef order theorem then gives equality of orders, without claiming the stronger quantitative estimate for this extension.

The effective-coefficient bounds follow from restrictions to projective fiber lines and lifted lines disjoint from the center; their converse realization by E and Q-hyperplanes is correct. Under the stated coefficient inequalities, beta remains in the fixed cone. Effectivity prevents rank gains on initially H-inactive blocks, while losing H strictly lowers rank. Thus blockwise losses cannot cancel, proving necessity and sufficiency of the two retention conditions. The explicit exceptional-removal examples satisfy these hypotheses and have the claimed jumps.

The supplied primary-source Poincare–Lelong evidence supports the normalization, curvature sign, local integrability, and divisor identities used here. Both summaries consistently describe the restricted theorem, its conditional Kähler extension, and its exclusion of arbitrary-background classification. No substantive gap or unmet completion criterion was found.

For arbitrary Kähler-source modifications, pulling back the actual divisor sections satisfies the approved Poincaré–Lelong premise; the resulting sandwich and task-given closed-nef order theorem prove equality, without asserting additional power bounds for that extension. Curve restrictions correctly establish the effective coefficient range, and exceptional and Q-hyperplane divisors realize it. reconstruction.statement:
Let X, its plain and blown factors Z_i, the integers m_i,ℓ_i,r_i, the fixed forms H_i,Q_i,κ_i, the fixed positive functions f_i,g_i, the fixed cone C_X and the effective ranks R_i,R be exactly those specified in w7-1/n2. All forms, line-bundle metrics and generating functions are fixed independently of ε, μ, h, divisors and cone parameters. Use dd^c=(i/(2π))∂∂̄. Every λ_μ below is defined using all smooth positive Gauduchon metrics; C_X is a restriction on backgrounds, not on test metrics. Smooth strictly positive probability volumes and smooth positive Hermitian perturbation forms are arbitrary.

1. Integer order. For every θ∈C_X and every such μ,h, there are 0<A≤B<∞ such that, for all 0<ε≤1,
A ε^(n−R(θ))≤V_μ(θ+εh)≤B ε^(n−R(θ)).
Thus a_−(θ)=a_+(θ)=n−R(θ). The family includes genuinely nonclosed backgrounds realizing orders 0 through n−1 with suitable choices of dimensions and products.

2. Modification equality. Starting with any such X, replace any collection of its plain P^(m_i) factors by Bl_(P^(ℓ_i))P^(m_i), with m_i≥2 and 0≤ℓ_i≤m_i−2, and leave all other factors unchanged. Let π:Y→X be the resulting product modification. On Y keep the pullbacks of the old fixed functions and forms and fix arbitrary strictly positive smooth functions for newly available Q generators. The pullback of C_X lies in this new fixed cone C_Y with zero coefficients on the new Q generators. For every θ∈C_X,
R_Y(π*θ)=R_X(θ),
a_−(π*θ)=a_+(π*θ)=a_−(θ)=a_+(θ)=n−R_X(θ).
Both X and Y have the quantitative two-sided volume bounds with this exponent, for independently arbitrary positive Hermitian perturbations and strictly positive probability volumes on the respective manifolds. Hence equality in both modification-order comparisons is unconditional for every background and every modification in this product-modification class, including degenerate genuinely nonclosed backgrounds.

More generally, let π:Y→X be any holomorphic modification of smooth compact n-folds with Y Kähler. Then, for every θ∈C_X and arbitrary μ_Y,h_Y on Y,
a_−(π*θ)=a_+(π*θ)=a_−(θ)=a_+(θ)=n−R(θ).
Here π*θ is smooth semipositive and π*θ+εh_Y is itself positive for every ε>0. With B_θ and φ_θ as defined in w7-1/n2, the function φ_θ∘π is globally locally integrable and, for some C,c>0,
π*θ≤Cπ*B_θ,
π*θ+dd^c(φ_θ∘π)≥cπ*B_θ
as pointwise forms and currents, respectively. For every Kähler form Ω_Y there are k,K>0, independent of 0<ε≤1, such that
k λ_(μ_Y)(π*B_θ+εΩ_Y)≤λ_(μ_Y)(π*θ+εh_Y)≤K λ_(μ_Y)(π*B_θ+εΩ_Y).
The smooth closed nef form π*B_θ has numerical dimension R(θ); more explicitly,
(π*B_θ)^(R(θ)+1)=0,
∫_Y (π*B_θ)^R(θ)∧Ω_Y^(n−R(θ))>0.
No assertion is made here for modifications with non-Kähler source outside the specified family.

3. Effective-divisorial residuals and their equality criterion. On each plain factor use O(H_i)=O(1) with its fixed Fubini–Study metric. On each blown factor use O(H_i)=π_i*O(1) and O(Q_i)=q_i*O(1), with their fixed pullback metrics. Pull these line bundles and metrics back to X. Consider tensor products
L_ν=⊗_i O(H_i)^(p_(νi)) ⊗ ⊗_(i blown) O(Q_i)^(q_(νi)),
where all exponents are integers, negative exponents are permitted, and each L_ν has its induced tensor-product metric. Let
D=∑_ν t_ν div(s_ν), t_ν≥0,
be a finite sum, where s_ν is a nonzero holomorphic section of L_ν. This specifies the allowed effective real divisor family, including arbitrary zero divisors in these linear systems, exceptional divisors and their nonnegative real sums. Its fixed smooth curvature representative and associated locally integrable function are
η_D=∑_i (δ_i H_i+ρ_i Q_i),
δ_i=∑_ν t_ν p_(νi), ρ_i=∑_ν t_ν q_(νi),
Φ_D=∑_ν t_ν log|s_ν|²,
with Q terms omitted on plain factors. They satisfy the exact current identity
[D]=η_D+dd^c Φ_D≥0.

The possible coefficient vectors of these effective real divisors are exactly those satisfying
δ_i≥0 on every plain factor;
δ_i≥0 and δ_i+ρ_i≥0 on every blown factor.
In particular these inequalities follow from effectivity, rather than being additional hypotheses. Conversely, every real coefficient vector in this range is realized by a divisor in the stated family. On a blown factor a pair (δ,ρ) in this range is realized by δE+(δ+ρ) times a Q-hyperplane divisor; on a plain factor a nonnegative δ is realized by δ times a hyperplane divisor.

Let θ∈C_X have the specified nonnegative parameters a_i,b_i,c_i,d_i. Suppose the explicit cone-preserving residual conditions hold:
a_i≥δ_i on every factor,
c_i≥ρ_i on every blown factor.
Set β=θ−η_D. Then β belongs to the same fixed cone C_X with parameters
(a_i′,b_i′,c_i′,d_i′)=(a_i−δ_i,b_i,c_i−ρ_i,d_i),
with Q parameters omitted on plain factors. In particular β is smooth semipositive and nef, and β+εh itself is positive for every ε>0 and every positive Hermitian h. A negative ρ_i is allowed. Moreover,
(θ−β)+dd^c Φ_D=[D]≥0,
so this is removal from an actual positive current.

Write a(ξ)=a_−(ξ)=a_+(ξ) for ξ∈C_X. Then
a(β)=n−R(β),
a(β)−a(θ)=∑_i [R_i(θ)−R_i(β)],
and R_i(β)≤R_i(θ) for every block. In particular both residual-order comparisons hold.

Equality in both comparisons, a_−(β)=a_−(θ) and a_+(β)=a_+(θ), holds if and only if both of the following conditions hold:
• For every initially H-active block, a_i−δ_i+b_i>0 whenever a_i+b_i>0.
• For every initially Q-only active blown block, c_i−ρ_i+d_i>0 whenever a_i=b_i=0 and c_i+d_i>0.
Thus every initially H-active block must retain H, and every initially Q-only active block must retain Q. On an H-active block, the Q coefficient may disappear or increase without affecting equality. If either retention condition fails, both residual-order inequalities are strict. The hypotheses a_i≥δ_i and c_i≥ρ_i are sufficient conditions for the residual to stay in this fixed cone, not an asserted characterization of nefness outside it.

4. Genuinely nonclosed examples and sharp divisorial removal. On Z=Bl_(P^ℓ)P^m, with m≥2, 0≤ℓ≤m−2 and r=m−ℓ−1, fix smooth g>0 with dg∧Q≠0. For every t>0 set θ_t=tH+gQ. This is genuinely nonclosed and smooth positive, with
θ_t≥min{t,min_Z g}(H+Q)>0,
a_−(θ_t)=a_+(θ_t)=0.
For every 0≤s≤t remove the effective divisor sE with the fixed curvature η_(sE)=s(H−Q). The residual is
β_s=(t−s)H+(g+s)Q.
It is smooth semipositive, nef and still genuinely nonclosed. Its orders are
 a_−(β_s)=a_+(β_s)=0 for 0≤s<t,
 a_−(β_t)=a_+(β_t)=m−r=ℓ+1.
Consequently equality after this removal holds exactly when s<t; at s=t the order jumps by ℓ+1. As ℓ ranges from 0 to m−2, these examples realize every jump 1,…,m−1.

The actual positive boundary current is
θ_t+dd^c(sψ_E)=s[E]+(t−s)H+(g+s)Q=s[E]+β_s≥0.
Removing s[E] from this chosen current leaves β_s, including the case s=t. All minimal perturbative divisorial multiplicities of θ_t and β_s vanish, so this actual boundary-current removal is distinct from perturbative minimal divisorial multiplicities.

For another example, let X=P^p×P^q, p,q≥1, and fix smooth f>0 depending nontrivially on the second factor. The background θ=fH_1 is genuinely nonclosed and has a_−(θ)=a_+(θ)=q. Every allowed product linear blowup, and more generally every holomorphic modification with Kähler source, preserves this order, including allowed blowups in active or inactive directions.

All conclusions and equality criteria are restricted to the stated fixed geometric, background and divisor families and the specified modifications; they do not assert an unrestricted integer-order theorem or an equality classification for arbitrary nonclosed nef backgrounds.
reconstruction.proof:
Use w7-1/n2 and its supporting result w7-1/n1. In using the supplied Poincaré–Lelong premise below, the line bundle always carries the specified smooth metric and the section is checked to be nonzero; thus the premise is used only in its stated scope.

1. Orders and the range of genuinely nonclosed examples. The quantitative bounds and integer order on C_X are exactly the conclusion of w7-1/n2, with arbitrary μ,h. For every total dimension n≥2, take a single blown factor with m=n. For an integer k between 1 and n−1, choose ℓ=k−1, so r=n−k, and fix g>0 with dg∧Q≠0 as constructed in that supporting note. Then gQ has order k. The same factor with the background H+gQ has order zero and the same nonzero exterior derivative. This proves the claimed existence of genuinely nonclosed examples of orders 0 through n−1 with suitable fixed geometric data. In dimension one every (1,1) form is top-degree and hence closed; the genuinely nonclosed existence assertion necessarily concerns dimensions at least two.

2. Product modifications. After replacing a plain factor by the specified blowup, its old H pulls back to the new H. Each old coefficient function pulls back to a smooth strictly positive function. Keeping these as the fixed old generators and giving the new Q generators zero coefficients embeds π*C_X into the new fixed cone C_Y. All backgrounds in this pullback cone are semipositive, and their positive perturbations are themselves positive.

An old H-active plain block had rank contribution m_i and, after the replacement, still has contribution m_i because it is H-active. An inactive plain block remains inactive, since its new Q coefficients are zero. Other blocks are unchanged. Therefore R_Y(π*θ)=R_X(θ). Apply w7-1/n2 separately on X and Y, with independently chosen volumes and Hermitian perturbations. Both give two-sided power estimates with exponent n−R_X(θ), proving equality in both order comparisons for every modification in this product class.

3. Arbitrary modifications with Kähler source. Let π:Y→X be a holomorphic modification and let Y be Kähler. The pulled-back background is smooth semipositive, so π*θ+εh_Y is positive for every ε>0. The pointwise upper inequality θ≤CB_θ pulls back to π*θ≤Cπ*B_θ.

The lower current inequality must be justified without assuming that arbitrary positive currents can be pulled back. Here φ_θ has the explicit logarithmic form from w7-1/n2, so this can be done directly. For every exceptional factor divisor used there, pull back its line bundle, metric and section s_(E_i) to Y. The pulled-back section is holomorphic and not identically zero: a modification is an isomorphism over a dense open set, and s_(E_i) is nonzero on a dense open set of X. By the supplied premise, log|π*s_(E_i)|² is locally integrable and
 dd^c log|π*s_(E_i)|²=[div(π*s_(E_i))]−π*H_i+π*Q_i.
Its left-hand potential is ψ_(E_i)∘π. Thus φ_θ∘π is globally locally integrable. Pull back the smooth semipositive terms in the block decomposition from w7-1/n2 and replace each integration current [E_i] by the positive current [div(π*s_(E_i))]. This proves
π*θ+dd^c(φ_θ∘π)≥cπ*B_θ.
In particular, the asserted current inequality has been established through actual holomorphic sections, rather than through an undefined pullback operation on currents.

The form B'=π*B_θ is smooth closed semipositive on the compact Kähler manifold Y. It is nef since B'+εΩ_Y is Kähler for every ε>0. Apply the comparison part of w7-1/n1 with B', π*θ, Ω_Y and the arbitrary h_Y,μ_Y. It gives precisely
kλ_(μ_Y)(B'+εΩ_Y)≤λ_(μ_Y)(π*θ+εh_Y)≤Kλ_(μ_Y)(B'+εΩ_Y),
with constants independent of 0<ε≤1. This is a full-Gauduchon comparison.

Put R=R(θ). The constant-rank identity on X gives B_θ^(R+1)=0, hence B'^(R+1)=0. On the dense open set where π is biholomorphic, B' has rank R. At every point of that set, B'^R∧Ω_Y^(n−R) is a strictly positive top-degree form (also when R=0). It is semipositive everywhere, so
∫_Y B'^R∧Ω_Y^(n−R)>0.
Thus the closed nef class of B' has numerical dimension R: its mixed intersection of degree R is positive, and all higher powers vanish. The closed-nef Kähler order theorem expressly permitted in the task gives common order n−R for B'. The preceding comparison changes log V by at most a bounded quantity, which vanishes after division by log ε. It follows that π*θ has the same two orders, equal to n−R. The equality with the orders of θ follows from part 1. No conclusion about a non-Kähler source is used or asserted.

4. Effective-divisor identities and the coefficient cone. Each L_ν is a holomorphic line bundle with a smooth induced tensor-product metric. Its curvature is
η_ν=∑_i p_(νi)H_i+∑_(blown i)q_(νi)Q_i,
including for negative exponents, since curvature of a dual is the negative curvature. Every s_ν is a nonzero holomorphic section. The supplied premise applies, including to singular zero divisors, and gives
 dd^c log|s_ν|²=[div(s_ν)]−η_ν.
Finite nonnegative real linear combinations prove global local integrability of Φ_D and the exact identity [D]=η_D+dd^cΦ_D with the coefficients stated in the note.

We next prove that effectivity forces exactly the claimed coefficient inequalities, rather than assuming the effective cone. Fix one nonzero section s of a tensor-product bundle with exponent vector (p_i,q_i). Choose a point of X where s is nonzero and, in every blown factor, outside E_i. Such a point exists because the nonzero locus is open and nonempty, and the complement of the finitely many exceptional divisors is dense. Hold all coordinates except those of one factor fixed. The restriction of s to any curve through this point is not identically zero. On a copy of P¹, the supplied premise, integrated against 1, says that the degree of the restricted line bundle is the nonnegative number of its section's zeros. The distributional dd^c term has integral zero. We apply this to the following curves.

On a plain block, a projective line through the chosen point has ∫H_i=1 and receives no other generator from that block. The other factors' forms restrict to zero. Its degree is p_i, proving p_i≥0.

On a blown block, the q-fiber is P^(ℓ_i+1). The map π on this fiber is the linear embedding [z:u]↦[z:u t]. A projective line in the fiber through the point therefore has H_i-degree 1 and Q_i-degree 0. It gives p_i≥0.

For the second inequality on a blown block, write the chosen point outside E_i as ([z:w],[w]) with w≠0. Choose a complex linear map A:C^(r_i+1)→C^(ℓ_i+1) with Aw=z. The map
[t]↦([At:t],[t])
is a holomorphic section of q_i whose image contains the chosen point. Both H_i and Q_i restrict to O(1) on this P^(r_i). Since r_i≥1, choose a projective line through the point in this section. Its degree for the restricted tensor-product bundle is p_i+q_i. It follows that p_i+q_i≥0.

These arguments check the nonzero-section hypothesis on each curve at the chosen point. Applying them to every s_ν, and taking the nonnegative weighted sums t_ν, gives δ_i≥0 on plain blocks and δ_i≥0, δ_i+ρ_i≥0 on blown blocks.

Conversely, any real vector satisfying these inequalities is realized in the specified family. On a plain block use δ_i times a hyperplane divisor, pulled back to X. On a blown block use
δ_i E_i+(δ_i+ρ_i)q_i^(−1)(a hyperplane).
Both coefficients are nonnegative. The exceptional divisor has bundle O(H_i)⊗O(Q_i)^(−1) with the fixed metric from w7-1/n2, and a q-hyperplane has bundle O(Q_i) with its fixed metric. Their total curvature is δ_i(H_i−Q_i)+(δ_i+ρ_i)Q_i=δ_iH_i+ρ_iQ_i. These are divisors of nonzero holomorphic sections of allowed bundles; pulling the sections back to X and summing over blocks completes the construction. Thus the coefficient-vector description is both necessary and sufficient within the stated divisor family. It does not claim that every effective divisor has a unique presentation.

5. Residual nefness and the equality criterion. Suppose the displayed cone-preserving inequalities hold. Subtracting η_D changes the parameters exactly to
(a_i−δ_i,b_i,c_i−ρ_i,d_i).
All these parameters are nonnegative, so β lies in the same cone with the same fixed generating functions. In particular it is smooth semipositive and nef, with β+εh positive for every ε>0. Also
(θ−β)+dd^cΦ_D=η_D+dd^cΦ_D=[D]≥0.
Thus the comparison indeed concerns removal from a positive current.

We verify blockwise that no effective rank can increase. If H was inactive, a_i=b_i=0. Since δ_i≥0 and δ_i≤a_i, necessarily δ_i=0, and H stays inactive. On a blown block with H inactive, effectivity then implies ρ_i≥0. If Q was also inactive, c_i=d_i=0 and ρ_i≤c_i force ρ_i=0, so the block remains inactive. If the block was Q-only, it can retain Q or lose it but cannot acquire H. If H was active, its old rank was m_i, the maximum block rank; retaining H keeps that rank, while losing H lowers it to at most r_i<m_i on a blown block, or to zero on a plain block. This proves R_i(β)≤R_i(θ) in every case, including when a negative ρ_i increases a Q coefficient on an originally H-active block.

By part 1,
a(β)−a(θ)=R(θ)−R(β)=∑_i(R_i(θ)−R_i(β)).
Every summand is nonnegative. On an originally H-active block it vanishes exactly when H is retained, which is precisely a_i−δ_i+b_i>0. On an originally Q-only block it vanishes exactly when Q is retained, namely c_i−ρ_i+d_i>0. On an originally inactive block it always vanishes. Therefore the sum is zero if and only if both retention conditions in the note hold. If either fails, the corresponding rank loss is strictly positive and no other block can compensate, so both order inequalities are strict. On an H-active block the fate of Q is irrelevant when H is retained. These are necessary and sufficient equality conditions under the stated cone-preserving residual hypotheses, not a characterization of nefness for backgrounds outside this cone.

6. Sharp removal and additional examples. Fix the blown factor and g>0 with dg∧Q≠0. For t>0,
θ_t=tH+gQ≥min(t,min_Z g)(H+Q)>0,
and dθ_t=dg∧Q≠0. It is an admissible, genuinely nonclosed member with H active, so it has order zero. The divisor sE, 0≤s≤t, has fixed curvature s(H−Q). Its residual is
β_s=(t−s)H+(g+s)Q.
It belongs to the same cone (the constant Q parameter increases by s), is semipositive and nef, and has the same nonzero exterior derivative. For s<t it is H-active and has order zero. At s=t it is Q-only with effective rank r, and has order m−r=ℓ+1. Thus equality holds exactly for s<t, with the claimed jump at the endpoint. The range 0≤ℓ≤m−2 gives every jump 1,…,m−1.

The logarithmic identity of w7-1/n2 gives, without approximation,
θ_t+dd^c(sψ_E)=s[E]+(t−s)H+(g+s)Q=s[E]+β_s≥0.
Removing the actual integration-current summand s[E] therefore leaves β_s. This is not a statement about forced singularities of a minimal representative. Indeed θ_t and every β_s are smooth semipositive: in every positive perturbation class they themselves, after adding the positive perturbation, supply smooth positive competitors with all divisorial Lelong numbers zero. Nonnegativity of such multiplicities gives vanishing of their minimal perturbative divisorial multiplicities, in accordance with the nef-background fact permitted in the task.

Finally, on P^p×P^q take a fixed positive f depending nontrivially on the second factor. Then df∧H_1≠0, so θ=fH_1 is genuinely nonclosed. Its effective rank is p and its order is q by part 1. Parts 2 and 3 prove preservation of this order under the specified product blowups and under every modification with Kähler source, whether the modified product block was active or inactive.

Every quantitative assertion above is inherited from the full-test proof in w7-1/n1 or from a comparison proved by pairing every Gauduchon test. The only closed-order theorem used is the one explicitly supplied in the task. All geometric forms, line-bundle metrics and coefficient functions remain fixed as stipulated. The results do not classify arbitrary nonclosed backgrounds, arbitrary residual nef cones, or modifications with non-Kähler source.
